report_name: OpenRouter Removes AI Providers After Private Prompts Leaked

threat_actors.name: Unnamed Attackers
threat_actors.description: Unidentified threat actors who compromised third-party AI inference providers, leading to the theft of stored user prompts from services like OpenRouter. The compromise was active since at least mid-July 2026.

attack_patterns.name: Supply Chain Compromise
attack_patterns.description: Attackers compromised third-party AI model providers, which are part of the supply chain for AI routing platforms like OpenRouter, to steal user data.

attack_patterns.name: Data from Cloud Storage
attack_patterns.description: Attackers exfiltrated improperly stored user prompts from the cloud infrastructure of third-party AI inference providers.

attack_patterns.name: Automated Exfiltration
attack_patterns.description: Attackers were actively accessing and stealing prompt data over a period of several months, suggesting an automated process for exfiltration.

attack_patterns.name: Credentials In Files
attack_patterns.description: In a related incident, Together AI accidentally leaked a private Hugging Face repository credential by committing it to a public GitHub repository, which was subsequently stolen and used by attackers.

attack_patterns.name: LLM Data Leakage
attack_patterns.description: Private user prompts and AI responses sent to third-party providers via OpenRouter were improperly stored and subsequently stolen by attackers, constituting a significant leakage of potentially sensitive data from the AI service.

identities.name: OpenRouter
identities.description: An AI request gateway platform that was impacted by a supply chain attack, where its third-party inference providers were breached, leading to the exposure of user prompts.

identities.name: Dragos
identities.description: An industrial cybersecurity firm that investigated and uncovered the data exposure by using canary tokens in prompts sent to various AI services.

identities.name: Together AI
identities.description: An AI provider that accidentally leaked a private Hugging Face repository credential to a public GitHub repository, contributing to the broader AI supply chain risk.

identities.name: Phala
identities.description: An AI provider that warned users about potential data exposure for prompts processed between October 21 and November 8.

identities.name: Hugging Face
identities.description: An AI platform whose private repository credential was accidentally leaked by Together AI.

identities.name: GitHub
identities.description: A public code repository where a private Hugging Face credential was accidentally leaked.

infrastructure.name: Compromised Third-Party Inference Provider Infrastructure
infrastructure.description: The cloud infrastructure of at least three third-party AI providers was compromised, allowing attackers to access and exfiltrate stored user prompts.

indicators.name: Canary Token Access Indicating Data Leakage
indicators.pattern:
title: Canary Token Access Indicating Data Leakage
id: 4b9f1c2d-e3a4-4b5c-8d6e-f7a8b9c0d1e2
status: experimental
description: >
  Detects DNS queries or web requests for canary token domains. This technique, used by Dragos in their investigation, can indicate that data containing the token has been stored and accessed, potentially signaling a data leak.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/11/openrouter-drops-3-providers-after.html
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-11-22
tags:
  - attack.t1530
level: medium
logsource:
  category: dns_query
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    QueryName|contains: '.canarytokens.org'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects access to canary tokens, a technique used by Dragos to identify the prompt leaks. This can be used by organizations to test their own AI providers for data retention and exposure.
